hypothesis: Running each GLM-5.3 prefill block through the dense matrices once (S rows) instead of once per token cuts coordinator prefill time without changing any token's result.
model: GLM-5.3-Flash (a community abliterated fine-tune; same architecture and tensor shapes), Colibri int4-gs64 streaming container, 195.8 GB
command: make -C c glm53; OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 COLI_CLUSTER_WEIGHTS=52,48 CLUSTER_WORKERS=<worker-a>:9100,<worker-b>:9100 GLM53_VERBOSE=1 ./glm53 --model <model> --prompt "$(cat prompt.txt)" --greedy 1 ; tok_s = 241 / (prefill seconds printed on stderr)

hardware.cpu: coordinator Intel i5-8500 (6C/6T); two expert workers Intel i5-4570 (4C/4T)
hardware.ram: coordinator 31 GB DDR4 dual channel; workers 15 GB each
hardware.storage: model on local SATA SSDs, ext4: coordinator Patriot P3 1 TB (~144 MB/s measured), workers ADATA SU650 (~371 MiB/s probe) and KingFast (~505 MiB/s probe)
hardware.os: coordinator Linux 7.1.13-hardened, gcc 16.2.1; workers Linux 7.1.8-arch / 7.0.0 Ubuntu, worker binary built with gcc 16 -march=haswell-native; Tailscale TCP between hosts; SCHED_IDLE background miners on all hosts

config.coordinator_build: d762a9dc (dev + GLM-5.3 cluster workers + worker read-ahead, per-token dense)
